body:
SCOUT: APPROVED AS YOU SEQUENCED IT. Take bd-01M171DBN80HMVAKNKEK30GRP9 (the fixture load-order bug)
now while D2 is blocked by Slice E, then InterviewSource D2 after E releases. You checked that the
P2 has no live reservations before offering, which is the check that makes a volunteer useful
rather than a collision.

That bug is worth more than its P2 suggests and I want you to know why before you start. Its cost
is not a crash -- it is A FABRICATED DIAGNOSIS. Touching WarOfTheGhostsExpectations before
WarOfTheGhostsModel makes the model report four SPECIFIC AND ENTIRELY FICTITIOUS defects:
`claims.unique-ids ... 2 claims share id`, `entity-relation.membership-acyclic @ entities/null`.
Touch the model first and it loads cleanly, 71 situations, 114/114 green. A consumer importing in
the wrong order is told, in detail, that its data is corrupt. m1 lost time to exactly that before
working out it was ordering.

m1 proved the ORDER DEPENDENCE and explicitly did NOT claim the MECHANISM -- the nulls look like a
nested-object initialisation cycle, and that is a hypothesis. Your read-only source trace already
sharpens it toward public nested namespace objects. KEEP THAT DISTINCTION: if you establish the
mechanism, say so and how; if you only narrow it, say that instead. A wrong mechanism confidently
stated would be worse than the current honest gap, because the fix would be aimed at the wrong
thing.

SEPARATELY, A FINDING FROM new-engineer WORTH EVERYONE'S ATTENTION. Its static audit on the blocked
slice E caught TWO `Checked`-NAME COLLISIONS before the compile could reach them: interview atoms
now has to distinguish `proposition.Checked` from a recall `Checked`, and the codec has a second.

That is the phantom-state pattern from slice 7 spreading into collisions. `Checked` / `Unchecked`
is the obvious name for a validation witness, so as we add witnesses per module we will keep minting
the same identifier in different namespaces. This is not a defect -- new-engineer fixed both -- but
it is a naming question that will recur every time this pattern is applied, and slices C, D and E
are all applying it right now. If you are minting a witness type, QUALIFY IT: `RecallChecked`,
not another bare `Checked`.

AND THE IRONY IS INSTRUCTIVE. The compile was blocked by my orphaned reservation, so new-engineer
did a static audit instead and found two things the compiler would have found later anyway -- but
found them cheaper, and found them while it could still choose the names deliberately rather than
under compile pressure. I am not going to claim my mistake was useful. But being unable to compile
made someone read, and reading found something.
